title: Erlang
subtitle: The concurrent, fault-tolerant functional language born in Ericsson's telephone switches, and the OTP framework built around it, from a first program to professional practice.
description: Erlang is a functional programming language designed at Ericsson from 1986 for telephone switches that had to handle many calls at once, survive hardware and software faults, and be upgraded without stopping. It was released as open source in 1998 together with OTP, its libraries and design patterns for reliable servers. Erlang runs on the BEAM virtual machine, which also runs Elixir and Gleam, and it powers message brokers such as RabbitMQ, messaging servers such as ejabberd, databases such as CouchDB, and the back ends of large chat and payment services.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. No functional programming background is needed. It starts with the shell and a first escript, works through terms, pattern matching, recursion, lists, maps and binaries, and then turns to what makes Erlang unique: processes, message passing, links, monitors and supervision trees, the OTP behaviours gen_server, supervisor and application, hot code loading and distribution, ending with a complete small project.

To run the code, install Erlang/OTP from [erlang.org/downloads](https://www.erlang.org/downloads), which links to installers for Windows and to package managers and source builds for macOS and Linux; the official Docker images are another option. There is no official online playground. Every complete program in these lessons is an escript that was run with `escript main.erl` on Erlang/OTP 29 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Meet Erlang's history and the BEAM, use the shell and escripts, and learn terms, single-assignment variables, pattern matching, functions, guards and recursion.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Work with lists, tuples, maps and binaries, then build concurrent programs from processes, mailboxes and selective receive, and make them robust with errors, links and monitors.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Structure systems with the OTP behaviours gen_server, supervisor and application, understand hot code loading and distribution, and build a complete supervised project with tests and the rebar3 toolchain.
